projects.title: Muninn
projects.tagline: Self-hosted stealth search and scrape gateway that hands AI agents a clean REST API.
projects.description: Muninn is a self-hosted search and data extraction API for a home server. A single persistent, anti-bot-hardened Chromium scrapes Google, Bing, DuckDuckGo and Mojeek behind a FastAPI gateway: a SQLite TTL cache with query hashing, an async FIFO request queue with a 15–30s throttler, and an engine manager that rotates engines round-robin and quarantines blocked ones for 30 minutes up to 12 hours, with state persisted across restarts. A separate /scrape worker tries plain HTTP first and only escalates to an isolated stealth-browser process on a block challenge, backed by SSRF guards, robots.txt checks, per-host rate limits and bounded caching.
projects.command: git clone https://github.com/reachdevel/Muninn.git && cd Muninn && make setup
setup: Linux only needs sudo for the browser-deps step; macOS is a no-op

projects.title: Lidless
projects.tagline: Blackout Mode drops every display and the keyboard backlight to dark while the Mac stays awake all night.
projects.description: Lidless lives in the menu bar and turns Blackout Mode on from a global shortcut. Every active display is driven to zero hardware brightness through DisplayServices, the keyboard backlight is switched off via CoreBrightness, and IOPMAssertion power assertions keep the system from ever idling — so overnight renders, downloads and builds keep running in a completely dark room. A listen-only CGEventTap watchdog ends Blackout Mode the moment you type or move the mouse past your threshold. Both private frameworks are resolved by name at runtime, so a future macOS reshaping degrades to a no-op instead of a crash.
setup: Grant Accessibility on first launch, then press the global shortcut (default CMD+F6)

projects.title: QBlocker4arm
projects.tagline: Hold-to-quit CMD+Q for Apple Silicon — a native arm64 port of QBlocker with zero dependencies.
projects.description: QBlocker stops you from quitting an app when you actually meant to close its window: CMD+Q is swallowed until you hold it down. Apple has confirmed macOS 27 is the last release with Rosetta, and the 2016 original could no longer compile on modern Xcode — so this fork is a full port to Swift 5 and arm64. CocoaPods is gone, along with DevMateKit and RealmSwift; the excluded-apps list moved to a small Codable store and the custom tab bar became a native NSTabViewController. LSSharedFileList login items gave way to SMAppService, Input Monitoring was added to the permission checklist, and the event tap now recovers on its own when macOS throttles it.
setup: Grant both Accessibility and Input Monitoring — without the latter CMD+Q is blocked silently
If macOS shows "Not Opened" with no Open Anyway, run the xattr command above

projects.title: opencode-git-commit
projects.tagline: Commits your working tree automatically when the OpenCode session goes idle.
projects.description: An OpenCode plugin that watches for the session.idle event and commits whatever is sitting in the working directory. It pulls the first line of your last assistant reply, sanitizes it, and uses it as the commit message so history reads like real work instead of a pile of snapshots; prefixes follow the Conventional Commits convention, and it runs git init for you when there is no repo yet. Written against the OpenCode v1.x plugin API and left unmaintained since v2 reshaped that surface — keep it pinned to v1.x, or port it.
setup: Targets OpenCode v1.x — the v2 plugin API is not compatible

projects.title: OmniCast TV
projects.tagline: Turns an Android TV into a wireless AirPlay and DLNA receiver for the phone and PC you already own.
projects.description: Start OmniCast TV once and your TV appears in the cast menu of your iPhone, iPad, Mac, Windows PC and Android apps. AirPlay — native C++ on the NDK, derived from UxPlay — handles screen mirroring with sound, AirPlay audio (ALAC, AAC-LC/ELD) and video-URL casting from Safari, QuickTime and Photos, played back by Media3. A Kotlin DLNA/UPnP MediaRenderer accepts pushes from VLC, BubbleUPnP, Plex, Windows "Cast to device" and any other UPnP controller, with on-screen transport controls. Everything runs on the local network: no account, no sign-in, no ads, no tracking and no cloud servers. It is built for the couch with Compose-for-TV D-pad navigation and clear focus states, starts automatically when the TV powers on, takes an editable receiver name such as "Living Room", supports optional PIN pairing, and only offers video the TV can actually decode — with specific error screens when it cannot. Miracast is out of reach because it needs the privileged CONFIGURE_WIFI_DISPLAY permission, Google Cast needs Google-issued device certificates, and DRM-protected streams show an explicit message rather than playing. Also ships a QR-code file sender for pushing photos, PDFs, video, audio or text straight to the TV. OmniCast TV is an independent app. AirPlay, iPhone, iPad, Mac and Safari are trademarks of Apple Inc., and DLNA is a trademark of the Digital Living Network Alliance; both are used only to describe compatibility. Not affiliated with or endorsed by Apple, DLNA or Google.
setup: The first build compiles OpenSSL 3.x for 3 ABIs (~2.5 min), then it is cached
On Android 10+ grant "Display over other apps" so a cast can open the player
Enable protocol tracing with: adb shell setprop debug.omnicast.log 1
